answer: A verifiable delay protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to continuously solve non-parallelizable sequential puzzles. An attacker creating a hollow fleet incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated CPU cores running uninterrupted per identity. Unproven nodes are confined to an execution island with restricted market access. A key limitation is that when verification beacons sweep past like a comet, connection latency can trigger false expirations for honest agents.
